note: Machine-readable freeze of the AB R3 logical contracts. Fraktal_AB_Part_III.md remains the normative prose; this file is the single artifact a generator, a gateway and a gate all read so the same field list is never transcribed twice. tools/check_ab_contracts.py enforces that the two agree.

int64.note: Declares, carries in a UDT and round-trips over CIP, but no arithmetic form compiles on this target. Accumulation belongs in the gateway.

float64.note: Studio rejects the declaration for this controller type. A Core value needing 64-bit float states its REAL precision loss in the contract or the controller leaves the baseline; narrowing it silently is forbidden.

bitstring32.note: masked; there is no distinct bit-string type

duration_ms.note: There is no native TIME or TIME32 on this target - the project will not import - so duration is integer milliseconds with a controller-side range check.

string.logix: STRING or a StringFamily type sized to the declared maximum

timestamp.unresolved: representation is not frozen; see openHoles

encodingRules: UDT member layout and array stride shall be derived from a measured stride for the target, never from member widths alone. On the pinned baseline a flat BOOL/SINT/INT/DINT/LINT/REAL type occupied 24 bytes with a 24-byte stride, four of them trailing padding forced by the LINT's 8-byte alignment.
NaN shall be detected by bit pattern or range, never by a self-comparison: the pattern transports faithfully over CIP but Logix ST evaluates NaN <> NaN as false.
Integer overflow wraps two's-complement with ReportMinorOverflow false, so range checking is the generator's responsibility.
Arrays are zero-based; a lower bound other than zero does not exist on this target.
STRING.LEN counts bytes. The UTF-8 policy above ASCII is not frozen; see openHoles.

capacities.derivationRule: Derived, not chosen: the whole request payload shall fit one unfragmented connected write at S1's conservative 500-byte connection size, so that no controller scan can fall between payload fragments. An operation needing more carries an operation ID plus a bounded argument set; large payloads are a staged configuration write, never a command.

capacityNote: Every S7 value was measured at exactly that capacity, not extrapolated: the fixture materialised these table sizes and the whole manifest was read from the controller. Raising one is a cost-curve calculation against AB_S7_MANIFEST_EVIDENCE.md, not a new spike - but the set shall be reviewed against a real station's module and field census before Phase 3, because FRK_MAX_FIELDS in particular is the first symbol a large station would exhaust.

openHoles.note: STRING.LEN was proved to count bytes, but only ASCII was written.

openHoles.item: timestamp and synchronization-quality representation as a generated member
coherence-token behaviour, freshness thresholds, poll budgets, quality/timestamp mapping
manifest table splitting and CIP fragmentation
commit-marker atomicity under a fragmented, batched or reordered transport write
openHoles.note: Both bindings assume every argument is visible to the scan before the commit marker is. AB removes fragmentation by bounding the payload to one connected write; TC3 has no equivalent bound. Untested in either. Test segmented writes, out-of-order argument commits, and a scan interleaved between argument and sequence writes before any writable deployment. The fallback - two-slot or seqlock - would apply to both bindings. Recorded in AB §7.7 and TC3 §3.10.

mailbox.commitRule: CommitSeq is nonzero, monotonic, and physically written last; it is the only commit marker. Transport write success is never command acceptance. This is the same commit-marker design TC3 uses, where the client writes all request arguments first and the Sequence last, so a defect here is a defect in both bindings.
mailbox.writeEnablement: The initial claim is read-only. Writes are switched on at the gateway by configuring a write root, which requires no controller download because the generated allow-list already gives root mailboxes read/write. Enabling a write root makes the transport command-capable and arms Core §14 in full: authenticated principals, least-privilege roles, and no anonymous write. A new project shall be asked explicitly which it is.

repositoryNegotiation.orderRule: No snapshot, discovery row, targeted read, subscription request, mutation or acknowledgement is accepted before ServerHello. Every later frame carries the selected version and ConnectionRevision.
